questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

An Country's Central News Agency (1)/ said the launch was a (2)/ "muscle-flexing". (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The word ‘country’ begins with a consonant so the article ‘an’ is incorrect here. The correct article here is ‘the’ as a particular country is being talked about.

questions.question:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

A total of 300 economically backward (1)/ students would being awarded (2)/ the Narendra Modi Scholarship. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 2 of the sentence as the verb ‘would’ does not fit here. The correct verb here is ‘were’ to denote past tense.

questions.question:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

I asked her if I ______ borrow her necklace for a day.
questions.solution: The correct word here is ‘could’ the past tense of ‘can.’ Only ‘could’ fits here.

questions.question:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

**She doesn't know ______ to accept or refuse the proposal.**
questions.solution: The correct word here is ‘whether’ which means ‘expressing a doubt or choice between alternatives.’ It fits here correctly.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.

Smear
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Smear=> coat or mark (something) messily or carelessly with a greasy or sticky substance

Discolor=> to remove the color

Honor=> high respect; great esteem

Laud=> praise

Upgrade=> raise (something) to a higher standard, in particular improve (equipment or machinery) by adding or replacing components

Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.

Concession
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Concession=>a thing that is granted, especially in response to demands

Denial=> refusal

Protest=> object

Retrograde=> directed or moving backwards

Allowance=> the amount of something that is permitted, especially within a set of regulations or for a specified purpose

Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.

Fickle
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Fickle=> changing frequently, especially as regards one's loyalties or affections

Cognizant=> having knowledge or awareness

Unstable=> not stable

Accidental=> happening by chance

Steadfast=> resolutely or dutifully firm and unwavering

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.

**Grudge**
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Grudge=> a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury

Spite=> a desire to hurt, annoy, or offend someone

Averse=> having a strong dislike of or opposition to something

Dislike=>feel distaste for or hostility towards

Goodwill=> friendly, helpful, or cooperative feelings or attitude

Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.

Hail
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• The meanings of the words are:
 
• **Hail** means pellets of frozen rain that fall in showers from cumulonimbus clouds
 
• **Rain **means water falling in drops from vapor condensed in the atmosphere
 
• **Storm **means a violent weather condition with winds 64-72 knots and precipitation and thunder and lightning
 
• **Greet **means give a polite word of recognition or sign of welcome when meeting (someone)
 
• **Dribble **means (of a liquid) fall slowly in drops or a thin stream

Thus **option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.

Incite
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Incite=> encourage or stir up (violent or unlawful behaviour)

Arouse=> evoke or awaken (a feeling, emotion, or response)

Drive=> propel or carry along by force in a specified direction

Prohibit=> formally forbid (something) by law, rule, or other authority

Thus option 4 is the correct antonym.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

With open arms
questions.solution: The idiom ‘with open arms’ means ‘cordially.’ Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

A bone of contention
questions.solution: The idiom ‘a bone of contention’ means ‘a reason of dispute.’ Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

No mention was made (to a) key amendment to the Constitution to accommodate demands that had been defeated just last Monday.
questions.solution: The correct preposition is ‘of’ as a mention is made ‘of’ something. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

Yet, it would be a mistake to presume that ties can so easily return to their pre-2015 strength, as the ground (had) shifted in too many ways since then.
questions.solution: The correct verb here is ‘has’ as present perfect tense is correct here. The other tenses are not correct here.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.

Amount paid to a man for his labour.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Incentive=> a thing that motivates or encourages someone to do something

Remuneration=> money paid for work or a service

Gratuity=> a sum of money paid to an employee at the end of a period of employment

Honorarium=> a payment given for professional services that are rendered nominally without charge

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.

A diplomatic representative in another country.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Spy=> a person employed by a government or other organization to secretly obtain information on an enemy or competitor

Spinster=> an unmarried woman, typically an older woman beyond the usual age for marriage

Bureaucrat=> an official in a government department, in particular one perceived as being concerned with procedural correctness at the expense of people's needs

Ambasador=> an accredited diplomat sent by a state as its permanent representative in a foreign country

Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: In the following question, a word has been written in four different ways out of which only one is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: The correct word is ‘secretary’ which means ‘a person employed by an individual or in an office to assist with correspondence, make appointments, and carry out administrative tasks.’ Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: In the following question, a word has been written in four different ways out of which only one is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: The correct word is ‘heinous’ which means ‘wicked.’

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Friendship

P: an asset

Q: in life

R: is indeed
questions.solution: R is the first statement as it has ‘is’ mentioned in it. P follows R as it states what it is. Q completes the statement by mentioning where it is an asset.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

If you don't want

P: freedom either

Q: you can't have

R: to take responsibility
questions.solution: R is the first statement as it states what one does not want. Q is the second statement as it starts mentioning the condition. P completes the statement by mentioning what one can’t have. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: **Poverty means ______of basic necessities**
questions.solution: The word ‘deprivation’ means ‘impoverishment’ and fits here correctly as poverty means unavailability of basic necessities. The word ‘appreciation’ means ‘recognition and enjoyment of the good qualities of someone or something’ and does not convey a proper meaning. The word ‘indulgence’ means ‘the action or fact of indulging’ and does not fit here.

questions.question: Poverty is mostly ______ in developing countries
questions.solution: The word ’prevalent’ means ‘widespread in a particular area or at a particular time’ and conveys the correct meaning that poverty is mostly found in developing countries. The words ‘irrelevant’ or ‘relevant’ do not fit in the context. The word ‘malevolent’ means ‘having or showing a wish to do evil to others’.

questions.question: Without ______food and nutrition,
questions.solution: The word here should be the correct adjective for food and nutrition. The word ‘adequate’ means ‘sufficient or enough’ and fits here correctly. The word here must convey a positive meaning.

questions.question: **Without proper ______ and toilets, they are forced**
questions.solution: The word ‘sanitation’ conditions relating to public health, especially the provision of clean drinking water and adequate sewage disposal’ and fits before the word ‘toilets.’ The word ‘inaction’ means ‘lack of action where some is expected or appropriate’ and ‘intuition’ means ‘the ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning’. Both the words do not fit in the context.

questions.question: **to ______ in open fields.**
questions.solution: The sentence talks about sanitation so the word ‘defecate’ which means ‘discharge faeces from the body’ fits here correctly. The word ‘abdicate’ means ‘renounce one's throne’ and ‘eliminate’ means ‘remove’. The word ‘allocate’ means ‘distribute (resources or duties) for a particular purpose’ and does not convey any meaning here. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.
